predecessors.name: Republic of Yemen
predecessors.text: Sa`dah Governorate, where the Houthis 'declared the creation of their own administration' on 26 March 2011

ledger.x: 19-26 March 2011: the Houthis set up their own administration in Sa`dah.
6 February 2015: the Houthis rule from Sanaa.
6 February 2015: 'the group was taking control of the country'.
22 July 2015: the Battle of Aden ends.

13 November 2020: the Houthis announce the capture of Camp Mas, 'which could open the way to the Raghwan and Midghal districts'; an earlier claim of advances in Mahliyah district (1 September 2020) was denied by the government.
1 April 2022: a UN-sponsored two-month nationwide truce begins and 'continued in practice' until October 2022; the war page dates it 2 April.
April 2022: the truce fixes the Houthi hold on western Marib.
11 September 2026: 'The Houthis recaptured Perim Island and then the Hanish Islands, completing their seizure of the Red Sea coast.'

wars.name: Houthi insurgency (2011 to 2014 phase)
wars.outcome: From the 2004 insurgency (18 June 2004 to the 2010 ceasefire, Houthis page) to March 2011, when the Houthis took Saada and declared their own administration; by November 2011 they held Al Jawf and northern Hajjah; they took Sanaa on 21 September 2014.

wars.name: Yemeni civil war
wars.outcome: From the Houthi takeover of Sanaa in September 2014; the Saudi-led coalition intervened on 27 March 2015; a UN truce began on 2 April 2022; on 7 April 2022 the Hadi government was dissolved in favour of a Presidential Leadership Council; the Houthis took…

wars.name: Marib campaign
wars.outcome: Camp Mas 13 November 2020; the offensive renewed 7-8 February 2021; claims of al-Abdiyah on 17 October 2021 (title only); a UN truce on 1 April 2022.

certainty.note: An insurgency's de facto control with no survey line: the governorate shapes are administrative proxies; the Marib, Taiz, Hodeidah and west-coast fronts moved without dates on the pages opened and are not drawn.
